intro: Tests used to, be used to, get used to, Past Simple, and Present Simple habits

items.q: When I was a child, I ___ walk to school every day, but now I take the bus.
items.why: used to describes a past habit that no longer happens

items.q: She ___ working night shifts now — she doesn't mind them at all.
items.why: be used to + gerund means she is now accustomed to it

items.q: It took him a few weeks, but he finally ___ driving on the left.
items.why: get used to + gerund describes the process of becoming accustomed

items.q: I usually ___ my keys on the kitchen table every evening.
items.why: Present Simple is correct for a current regular habit

items.q: Last summer, the electricity ___ during the storm on Tuesday night.
items.why: Past Simple is used for a single completed past event

parts.title: Complete the sentences with the correct form.

items.post: a pipe every evening when he was young, but he quit decades ago.
items.why: used to + infinitive for a past habit that stopped

items.pre: After moving to a cold country, she slowly
items.post: waking up in the dark every morning.
items.why: get used to + gerund for the process of becoming accustomed

items.post: dinner late because their parents always worked long hours.
items.why: be used to + gerund for a current state of being accustomed

items.why: Past Simple for a single completed event in the past

items.why: Present Simple for a current repeated habit

items.post: alone at first, but eventually I started enjoying it.
items.why: be used to + gerund following a modal construction

parts.title: Find and correct the mistake in each sentence.

items.sentence: When he moved abroad, he couldn't get used to eat such spicy food.
items.corrected: When he moved abroad, he couldn't get used to eating such spicy food.
items.why: get used to must be followed by a gerund, not a bare infinitive

items.sentence: She used to works in a bakery before she became a teacher.
items.corrected: She used to work in a bakery before she became a teacher.
items.why: used to is always followed by the bare infinitive, not a conjugated verb

items.sentence: I am used to wake up early because my job starts at six.
items.corrected: I am used to waking up early because my job starts at six.
items.why: be used to must be followed by a gerund, not a bare infinitive

parts.title: Write your own sentences.
parts.pointsLabel: 2 points: 1 for correct form, 1 for meaning and use

items.prompt: Write one sentence about something you used to do as a child but no longer do now.
items.criteria: Accept sentences using used to + bare infinitive referring to a past habit that has stopped; present tense contrast is a bonus
items.example: I used to collect football stickers when I was young, but I stopped when I turned twelve.

items.prompt: Write one sentence about something that was difficult at first but that you are now used to doing in your daily life.
items.criteria: Accept sentences using be used to or get used to + gerund, showing familiarity with something that took adjustment
items.example: I got used to commuting by bicycle after a few months, and now I actually enjoy it.
